code-buddy.summary: A code-review platform I architected at Qualcomm, connecting issue detection, candidate fixes, and validation for 12,000+ engineers across 4,000+ repositories.
code-buddy.overview: Code Buddy reviews code changes inside the engineering workflow, where a useful finding needs enough context to explain the problem and propose a fix. I architected the platform at Qualcomm around separate detection, repair, and validation steps coordinated through tool calls. Structural retrieval supplies relevant symbols and dependencies, and candidate changes pass validation guardrails before a review is posted. The platform grew from a pilot to more than two million automated reviews. My work also included an evaluation harness for comparing review quality as prompts and models changed.

cabinai.summary: A driving-assistant prototype combining camera-based driver monitoring, voice, gestures, and local retrieval through seven coordinated components.
cabinai.overview: CabinAI brings driver monitoring and cabin interaction into one working demo. Camera frames produce face and hand landmarks, which feed drowsiness heuristics and gesture recognition. A shared event bus connects that state to voice requests, local knowledge retrieval, and a driving simulator. Known cabin commands take a deterministic path; an explicit routing policy sends more complex questions to a language model. I built and presented the prototype as a solo SparQ 2026 entry, winning the Jury Award among 166 teams.

healthsense.summary: An experimental biosignal dashboard combining ECG classification, signal-processing heuristics, and explanations across five sensor streams.
healthsense.overview: HealthSense explores how ECG, EEG, PPG, EMG, and motion signals can share one analysis interface. The implemented pipeline combines signal-processing heuristics with a small PyTorch convolutional model for ECG classification, exported for ONNX Runtime inference. Agent components organize the results and provide explanations in the dashboard. I also used simulated adaptation curves to demonstrate how a future personalization workflow could appear. The completed work is a systems prototype and a small ECG experiment, with clinical validation and on-device training still to be done.

cliffside-conquest.summary: A Unity game prototype centered on character movement through a cliffside environment, documented in a gameplay walkthrough.
cliffside-conquest.overview: Cliffside Conquest is a Unity prototype built around moving a character through a cliffside level. The scene combines the player, terrain, and visual feedback in a playable environment. The gameplay walkthrough shows the movement and interactions implemented in the level.

myai.summary: An offline Android assistant that checks keywords, cached answers, and local tools before invoking a quantized language model through Qualcomm Genie.
myai.overview: MyAI explores how much a personal assistant can do directly on a phone. Simple requests use deterministic matching, previously accepted answers, or tools for calculations, dates, calendar events, contacts, and alarms. Requests that need generation reach a local model through Qualcomm Genie. I tested a quantized Qwen bundle on Snapdragon 8 Elite and connected structured model output to the tool layer. The default Android app omits INTERNET permission, and a Gradle check prevents the permission from being added accidentally.

digital-twin-mapmyindia.summary: A Unity map viewer with location initialization, coordinate-based navigation, and animated transitions between distant places.
digital-twin-mapmyindia.overview: This project turns geographic coordinates into a navigable Unity scene. A location provider initializes the map, while mouse-look, movement, rotation, and zoom controls let a user explore the area. To move between distant coordinates, a C# coroutine first zooms out, interpolates the map center, and restores the destination zoom. That sequence keeps the transition understandable as the map changes. The original title and recording use MapMyIndia terminology; the public implementation uses Mapbox Unity components and represents a geographic viewer rather than a live synchronized digital twin.

compiler-construction.summary: A team-built compiler front end in C covering lexical analysis, LL(1) parsing, AST construction, scoped symbol tables, and partial semantic analysis.
compiler-construction.overview: Our team built a compiler front end to understand how source text becomes a structured program representation. A hand-written lexer produces tokens, and a table-driven LL(1) parser reads grammar productions and computes FIRST and FOLLOW sets. A separate pass reduces the parse tree to an abstract syntax tree. Symbol tables then track declarations, types, scopes, and offsets for semantic checks. The implementation includes panic-mode error recovery so parsing can continue after malformed input. Executable code generation was outside the completed implementation.

live-train-status.summary: A Flutter railway prototype backed by relational queries for trains, ordered stops, schedules, routes, and delay updates.
live-train-status.overview: Live Train Status connects a database-systems project to a mobile interface. The SQL schema models trains, stations, schedules, routes, and delays, while queries and views derive possible journeys and arrival estimates. Flutter screens fetch JSON data for train lookup and status views, with a separate administrative flow for delay updates. The project let me work through the full path from relational data modeling to asynchronous mobile presentation. The repository preserves the schema and app; the original external backend is not maintained as a live railway service.

florafast-plant-delivery-app.summary: A Flutter plant-shopping prototype with Firebase email authentication, product browsing, favorites, and cart interactions.
florafast-plant-delivery-app.overview: FloraFast follows the main steps of a mobile shopping experience: create an account, browse a plant catalog, open a product, save favorites, and add items to a cart. Firebase Authentication handles email sign-up, sign-in, and password resets. Product screens share a static plant model with local favorite and cart state. I used the project to develop reusable Flutter screens and connect account flows to a broader application. The scan screen is a visual prototype; plant recognition, checkout, and persisted shopping data were not implemented.

iworkslab-food-delivery-app.summary: A Flutter food-store prototype with shared product, cart, and order state built using Provider and ChangeNotifier.
iworkslab-food-delivery-app.overview: This app connects product browsing to a cart and order history through a shared state model. Users can save products, change quantities, inspect totals, and submit the current cart to the order view. Provider and ChangeNotifier keep these interactions consistent across screens, while reusable widgets support the login, catalog, and product layouts. The project focuses on application state and responsive presentation. Its catalog, authentication screens, and orders use local demo data; backend persistence, payment processing, and fulfillment are outside the implementation.

wisewaterman-water-conservation-game-for.summary: A browser-playable Unity learning game that connects a water-powered jetpack to questions about water conservation.
wisewaterman-water-conservation-game-for.overview: WiseWaterman makes water conservation part of the game rules. Players navigate obstacles using a jetpack with a limited water supply and collect question boxes along the route. Correct answers replenish the meter, while feedback explains the conservation lesson. The game was developed for an NCERT-funded effort overseen by Prof. Neetu Yadav. My contributions covered game design, animation, audio production, and writing. The published WebGL build and walkthrough show the playable experience; the public repository contains compiled game assets rather than the Unity source project.

uno-game.summary: A Java Swing UNO game built as a team course project, with deck management, turn tracking, and action-card rules.
uno-game.overview: Our team used UNO to work through object-oriented modeling and event-driven desktop programming. Java classes represent cards, the deck, player hands, and the current game state, while a Swing interface presents the hand and available actions. The game coordinator tracks legal color and value, direction, and the active player. Skip, reverse, draw, and wild cards introduce rule changes that have to stay consistent with the interface. The project demonstrates a playable course implementation, with the rules and Swing presentation still closely coupled.

igcsm-life-cycle-anaysis.summary: A HoloLens research application for inspecting an e-bicycle and comparing life-cycle assessment scenarios in mixed reality.
igcsm-life-cycle-anaysis.overview: During DAAD-supported research at TU Braunschweig, our team explored how mixed reality could make life-cycle assessment data easier to inspect. The HoloLens application places an e-bicycle and its assessment information in a spatial interface. Users can navigate the model, select product scenarios, and compare carbon emissions across the product lifetime. I worked on the application and interaction flow with collaborators at TU Braunschweig and BITS Pilani, then demonstrated the experience to a scientific jury. The work focused on presenting assessment data and scenario comparisons through spatial interaction.

decentralized-academic-certificate-syste.summary: A React and Solidity document-registry prototype that stores files on IPFS and records their content hashes on Ethereum.
decentralized-academic-certificate-syste.overview: This project separates document storage from the record used to check its contents. A React interface uploads a file to IPFS, then writes its content hash and metadata to a Solidity contract through Web3. The interface can list registry entries and retrieve the corresponding document. Truffle and Ganache support local contract deployment, and tests cover upload and input validation. The implementation demonstrates a tamper-evident file registry. A matching hash establishes document integrity; accredited issuers, certificate revocation, and private access would need additional mechanisms.

simulation-of-delhi-s-air-pollution.summary: A COMSOL numerical study of vehicular carbon-monoxide dispersion across a 50 × 50 km Delhi region.
simulation-of-delhi-s-air-pollution.overview: Our numerical-analysis team studied how vehicle emissions disperse under different wind and obstacle conditions. We used an advection-diffusion model in COMSOL Multiphysics to represent transport and spreading, then inspected concentration contours as the simulation evolved. After comparing the model behavior under different conditions, we applied the setup to a Delhi case study. The report records the assumptions, numerical setup, and resulting concentration patterns. The project is a simulation study whose results depend on those assumptions, rather than a measured map or a real-time air-quality forecast.

art-gallery.summary: An augmented-reality gallery prototype that recognizes physical artwork and presents related digital content in the surrounding space.
art-gallery.overview: Built during my AR development work at Invoxel, Art Gallery uses image recognition to connect physical artworks with digital content. Recognizing an artwork brings its related material into the AR scene, where visitors can view it alongside the physical image. The recorded walkthrough shows the recognition and content-display sequence.

adoption-app.summary: An early Flutter interface prototype for browsing pets, with reusable cards, horizontal lists, and nearby and wishlist sections.
adoption-app.overview: Adoption App was an early exercise in composing a mobile browsing interface from reusable Flutter widgets. The home screen combines a greeting, search field, nearby section, and horizontal pet-card lists. Sample content supplies the images and information needed to develop the layout. The work focused on screen composition, spacing, and repeated card structures, with placeholder interactions used to explore the flow. It does not connect to an adoption service, perform real search, or maintain a persistent wishlist.

notes-app.summary: A Flutter notes app connecting Google sign-in to Cloud Firestore and live create, edit, and delete workflows.
notes-app.overview: Built during ACM Summer Explore at BITS Pilani, Notes App put authentication and asynchronous data into a small mobile application. Google sign-in opens the account flow, and a Cloud Firestore collection supplies the note grid through a live snapshot stream. Separate screens handle creating and editing notes, while deletion updates the collection and the displayed list. The project helped me connect mobile navigation, editable forms, and remote data updates in one application. The interface reflects database changes without requiring a manual refresh.

other-projects-on-github.summary: A source archive of smaller mobile apps, programming coursework, utilities, and experiments alongside the featured projects.
other-projects-on-github.overview: My GitHub archive includes smaller Flutter apps, programming exercises, utilities, and experiments alongside the featured case studies. These repositories trace my work from individual mobile screens and course assignments to larger systems. Open the profile to inspect each project’s source, documentation, and history, including its scope and level of completeness.

kxr-smithy-simulation.summary: A virtual workshop prototype developed through the Kalipatnapu AR/VR Lab to present a smithy process as an interactive scene.
kxr-smithy-simulation.overview: Developed through the Kalipatnapu AR/VR Lab at BITS Pilani, this simulation presents a smithy workshop as a virtual environment. Users explore the scene and follow an interactive presentation of the workshop process. The recording shows how the environment and sequence fit together in the demonstration.

hand-tracking.summary: A spatial-interaction prototype that maps tracked hand movement to responses in a virtual scene.
hand-tracking.overview: Hand Tracking connects physical hand movement to responses in a virtual scene. The prototype explores direct spatial input and the visual feedback needed to show what the system has recognized. The recorded demonstration follows the interaction from the user’s hand motion to the resulting scene response.

campus-navigation.summary: An AR wayfinding prototype exploring how campus route guidance can appear within a spatial interface.
campus-navigation.overview: Campus Navigation explores how route guidance can appear within an augmented-reality view. The prototype presents campus wayfinding through a spatial interface, connecting navigation instructions to the surrounding scene. The walkthrough follows the guidance flow as implemented in the demo; campus-wide positioning and route coverage were not validated.

measure-tape.summary: An AR measurement prototype for selecting points in a scene and displaying the distance between them.
measure-tape.overview: Measure Tape brings point-to-point measurement into an AR view. Users select positions in space and see the distance displayed within the scene. The recorded walkthrough follows point selection and the resulting measurement. The project focuses on spatial input and visual feedback; it has not been calibrated as a precision measuring instrument.
